claim: Bootstrap registers: GVCP capability 0x0934 (bit 0x00080000 IEEE1588, 0x00020000 scheduled action, 0x00000040 action, 0x00100000 unconditional action); configuration 0x0954 bit 0x00080000 = IEEE1588 enable; 0x096C IEEE1588 status (low 4 bits); 0x0970 scheduled action queue size; action device key 0x090C; action group key/mask 0x9800+0x10*i / 0x9804+0x10*i; timestamp control 0x0944 (1=reset, 2=latch), value 0x0948/0x094C.

GVCP ACTION_CMD (0x0100, ack 0x0101) packet: 8-byte header [0x42, flags (0x80=scheduled action time present, 0x01=ack required), cmd u16, length u16 (12 or 20), req_id u16] followed by device_key u32, group_key u32, group_mask u32, optional action_time u64, big-endian, UDP port 3956. Late scheduled actions are reported with status 0x8016 ACTION_LATE.
how_verified: read-code + ran-test: python -I gev_ptp_sync_test.py selftest --pcap action_cmds.pcap; tshark 4.2.2 -r action_cmds.pcap -d udp.port==3956,gvcp -V decoded Flags 0x81, Scheduled Action Command True, Device Key 0x12345678, Group Key 1, Mask 1, Action Scheduled Time 0x000001e23f5a1000 (log: ptp-sync-tests/out/docker_run_final.log)

claim: pypylon exposes action commands and scheduled action commands from Python: IGigETransportLayer.ActionCommand(...) and .ScheduledActionCommand(deviceKey, groupKey, groupMask, actionTimeNs, broadcastAddress) with IssueNoWait()/IssueWait().

GenTL SFNC 1.2 defines Interface-module action features (ActionCommand, ActionDeviceKey, ActionGroupKey, ActionGroupMask, ActionScheduledTimeEnable, ActionScheduledTime, GevActionDestinationIPAddress); harvesters 1.4.3 exposes the Interface module node_map via ImageAcquirer.interface.
pyGigEVision v0.2.2 (2026-07-08) implements only DISCOVERY, FORCEIP, READ/WRITE REG/MEM and PACKETRESEND GVCP commands - no ACTION_CMD or PTP features - but parses the 64-bit GVSP leader timestamp.

Grandmaster selection is by the IEEE 1588 Best Master Clock Algorithm among the cameras (Basler: lowest Priority1 wins; Allied Vision PtpMode=Auto; LUCID BMC + PtpSlaveOnly), so no host master is required; without a GPS/UTC grandmaster the shared timescale is arbitrary.

Windows' built-in PTP (w32time ptpprov) is a client/subordinate only (Windows 10 1809+/Server 2019+); multicast receive is off by default (EnableMulticastRx) and masters are configured in PtpMasters. No Microsoft source describes Windows as a PTP master.
how_verified: read-code/doc (W32Time repo cloned; Validation Guide .docx text-extracted)

claim: On Linux, linuxptp ptp4l can be the grandmaster: defaults UDPv4, E2E, hardware timestamping, priority1 128; -S software timestamping; serverOnly prevents entering client state; event/general ports 319/320 multicast 224.0.1.129 (P2P 224.0.0.107). linuxptp is Linux-only by design.
IGMP snooping blocks Basler GigE camera PTP traffic (sent to 224.0.1.129) because the cameras don't join an IGMP group; Basler's only fix is to disable IGMP snooping.

Vendor sync accuracy figures: Allied Vision 'within two microseconds', <±1 µs max offset over 69 h, ~125 ns on scope between two cameras; Teledyne 'within a few microseconds'. Allied Vision found host software PTP masters on Windows/Linux gave 'significant jitter'.
how_verified: read-spec/doc (AV app note V1.3.1 2025-02-18 via pdftotext)

claim: Scheduled action procedure: sync PTP, TimestampLatch on one camera, read TimestampLatchValue, send action with action_time = value + delay (ticks = ns with PTP); 0 or past time executes immediately (Basler); cameras configured TriggerSelector=FrameStart, TriggerMode=On, TriggerSource=Action1 with ActionDeviceKey/ActionSelector/ActionGroupKey/ActionGroupMask (SFNC §14 example).

Vendor PTP-based synchronous acquisition modes: Basler Synchronous Free Run (SyncFreeRunTimerStartTimeLow/High, SyncFreeRunTimerTriggerRateAbs, SyncFreeRunTimerUpdate, SyncFreeRunTimerEnable); LUCID PTPSync (AcquisitionStartMode=PTPSync, PTPSyncFrameRate < AcquisitionFrameRate; firmware schedules 4 advance action commands); Allied Vision PtpAcquisitionGateTime gating FixedRate triggers until GevTimestampValue >= gate time.

Every GVSP image leader carries a 64-bit device timestamp; Aravis converts it to ns using GevTimestampTickFrequency read once at stream creation, so PTP (which changes Basler tick from 125 MHz to 1 GHz) should be enabled before creating the stream. The Aravis fake camera stamps frames with host wall-clock time.
